title: The Significance of the Irritative Zone in Presurgical Epilepsy Diagnostics
summary:
Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder. While many patients become seizure-free with medication, some do not respond sufficiently to medical treatment. For these individuals, epilepsy surgery may represent a possible treatment option. However, successful surgery requires the precise identification of the brain region from which the seizures originate.

This study investigates the contribution of video-EEG monitoring (VEM), particularly the role of the so-called irritative zone, in presurgical epilepsy diagnostics. The aim is to improve the planning of epilepsy surgery and thereby enhance patient counseling regarding possible treatment outcomes.
conditions: Localization-related (focal)(partial) symptomatic epilepsy and epileptic syndromes with complex partial seizures

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of data from patients who were admitted to the video-EEG monitoring unit of the Epilepsiezentrum Hessen over a 10-year period (2015–2024). The analysis will be conducted based on the patient logs maintained in the video-EEG monitoring unit.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who received treatment between 2015 and 2024
Exclusion criteria:
Patient age < 18 years
